points.description: States that a higher priority process/task is prevented from running / does not get the CPU (is blocked or made to wait).
States that this happens because of / is caused by a lower priority process (the lower priority process effectively runs or blocks the higher one).
States that the lower priority process holds a resource (e.g. lock/shared resource) that the higher priority process needs, which is the cause.
points.partial_credit: 0.5 if resource holding is mentioned but the higher priority process's need for it or the link to blocking is not stated clearly

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three elements stated precisely: higher priority process denied the CPU, caused by a lower priority process, because that lower priority process holds a resource. Generic answers like "priorities get mixed up" or "low priority runs before high priority" without the resource-holding cause earn nothing on P3. Reversed priorities or a wrong cause (e.g. deadlock, starvation by many processes) earn nothing on the affected point.
